definition: A microfold cell that is part of the epithelium of the palatine tonsil, a nasopharynx-associated lymphoid tissue of Waldeyer's ring. Like other microfold cells it has a reduced or absent apical brush border (the 'microfold' surface), a thin or absent glycocalyx and mucus layer, and a basolateral pocket enclosing dendritic cells, macrophages and lymphocytes; it transcytoses luminal antigen across the tonsil crypt (follicle-associated, reticulated) lymphoepithelium to the underlying lymphoid tissue. Because tonsils lack afferent lymphatics, this crypt microfold-cell epithelium is a principal portal delivering inhaled and ingested antigen to the mucosal immune system, initiating IgA and germinal-center responses. It expresses the conserved microfold-cell program (SPIB, SOX8, GP2, MARCKSL1) and is detected histologically by cytokeratin 8/18 (CK8/18); no single marker is definitive. It is a distinct antigen-transporting cell type co-resident with, but separate from, the crypt reticulated epithelial cell.

logical_axioms.notes: Resides in the crypt (reticulated) epithelium of the palatine tonsil.
Transcytoses luminal antigen across the tonsil crypt epithelium.
Delivers antigen to sub-epithelial lymphoid tissue, initiating mucosal immunity.

references.supports: Human adenoid (NALT, Waldeyer's ring) M cells resolved as distinct immature/mature clusters from progenitor club cells; share a common gene set with palatine-tonsil M cells and gut/airway M cells.
Human tonsil atlas: M-cell markers (SPIB, MARCKSL1) in only a minority (<20%) of 'crypt' epithelial cells; no discrete M-cell cluster annotated (under-resolved).

Palatine tonsil scRNA: markers previously used for tonsil/adenoid M cells (class II beta-tubulin, clusterin) broadly expressed across epithelial cells with NO cluster showing a specific M-cell signature; antigen entry may be partly passive or myeloid-mediated.
CK8/18 (cytokeratin 8/18) is a practical histological marker for microfold cells in human tonsillar epithelium.
Conserved SOX8-dependent M-cell maturation program shared across MALT.
Cross-MALT conservation of the M-cell transcriptional program (gut/airway).

justification: Intended DIRECT PARENT is the proposed general 'microfold cell' term (companion NTR #3684); parent is set provisionally to epithelial cell (CL:0000066) here because the general term does not yet exist. Palatine-tonsil M cells are long established by ultrastructure and immunohistology and share the conserved M-cell program, BUT their transcriptomic status is currently contested/under-resolved: (i) in the Massoni-Badosa tonsil atlas SPIB/MARCKSL1 appear in <20% of 'crypt' epithelial cells with no discrete M-cell cluster; (ii) De Martin et al. 2023 found proposed tonsil/adenoid M-cell markers broadly expressed with no cluster showing a specific M-cell signature (suggesting partly passive or myeloid-mediated antigen entry); whereas (iii) the related adenoid (NALT) does resolve distinct immature/mature M-cell clusters (Alvarez-Arguedas 2025). Curators should note this cell may be rare/short-lived or transcriptionally blended in the palatine tonsil and is best defined by location + function + marker combination rather than a single clean scRNA cluster. It is a DISTINCT co-resident cell type of the crypt reticulated epithelium — NOT a subtype of the crypt epithelial cell (see #3682). Species-neutral; GP2/SPIB/SOX8/MARCKSL1 kept textual.

## New term request: microfold cell of palatine tonsil

**Proposed label:** microfold cell of palatine tonsil

**Definition:** A microfold cell that is part of the epithelium of the palatine tonsil, a nasopharynx-associated lymphoid tissue of Waldeyer's ring. Like other microfold cells it has a reduced or absent apical brush border (the 'microfold' surface), a thin or absent glycocalyx and mucus layer, and a basolateral pocket enclosing dendritic cells, macrophages and lymphocytes; it transcytoses luminal antigen across the tonsil crypt (follicle-associated, reticulated) lymphoepithelium to the underlying lymphoid tissue. Because tonsils lack afferent lymphatics, this crypt microfold-cell epithelium is a principal portal delivering inhaled and ingested antigen to the mucosal immune system, initiating IgA and germinal-center responses. It expresses the conserved microfold-cell program (SPIB, SOX8, GP2, MARCKSL1) and is detected histologically by cytokeratin 8/18 (CK8/18); no single marker is definitive. It is a distinct antigen-transporting cell type co-resident with, but separate from, the crypt reticulated epithelial cell.

**Parent (is_a):** epithelial cell (CL:0000066)

**Anatomical location:** tonsil epithelium (UBERON:0013696)

**Logical axioms:**
- `part of` (BFO:0000050) some **tonsil epithelium** (UBERON:0013696) — Resides in the crypt (reticulated) epithelium of the palatine tonsil.
- `capable of` (RO:0002215) some **transcytosis** (GO:0045056) — Transcytoses luminal antigen across the tonsil crypt epithelium.
- `capable of part of` (RO:0002216) some **mucosal immune response** (GO:0002385) — Delivers antigen to sub-epithelial lymphoid tissue, initiating mucosal immunity.

**Synonyms:**
- M cell of palatine tonsil (exact)
- tonsil microfold cell (exact)
- Waldeyer's ring M cell (related)

**References:**
- Alvarez-Arguedas et al. (2025). DOI: 10.1016/j.mucimm.2025.07.006 ; PMID:40721095 — Human adenoid (NALT, Waldeyer's ring) M cells resolved as distinct immature/mature clusters from progenitor club cells; share a common gene set with palatine-tonsil M cells and gut/airway M cells.
- Massoni-Badosa et al. (2024). DOI: 10.1016/j.immuni.2024.01.006 ; PMID:38301653 — Human tonsil atlas: M-cell markers (SPIB, MARCKSL1) in only a minority (<20%) of 'crypt' epithelial cells; no discrete M-cell cluster annotated (under-resolved).
- De Martin et al. (2023). DOI: 10.1038/s41590-023-01502-4 ; PMID:37202490 — Palatine tonsil scRNA: markers previously used for tonsil/adenoid M cells (class II beta-tubulin, clusterin) broadly expressed across epithelial cells with NO cluster showing a specific M-cell signature; antigen entry may be partly passive or myeloid-mediated.
- Perry et al. (2025). DOI: 10.1128/jvi.01460-24 ; PMID:39791909 — CK8/18 (cytokeratin 8/18) is a practical histological marker for microfold cells in human tonsillar epithelium.
- Kimura et al. (2019). DOI: 10.1084/jem.20181604 ; PMID:30877171 — Conserved SOX8-dependent M-cell maturation program shared across MALT.
- Han (2024). DOI: 10.1165/rcmb.2024-0002ED ; PMID:38301262 — Cross-MALT conservation of the M-cell transcriptional program (gut/airway).

**Justification:** Intended DIRECT PARENT is the proposed general 'microfold cell' term (companion NTR #3684); parent is set provisionally to epithelial cell (CL:0000066) here because the general term does not yet exist. Palatine-tonsil M cells are long established by ultrastructure and immunohistology and share the conserved M-cell program, BUT their transcriptomic status is currently contested/under-resolved: (i) in the Massoni-Badosa tonsil atlas SPIB/MARCKSL1 appear in <20% of 'crypt' epithelial cells with no discrete M-cell cluster; (ii) De Martin et al. 2023 found proposed tonsil/adenoid M-cell markers broadly expressed with no cluster showing a specific M-cell signature (suggesting partly passive or myeloid-mediated antigen entry); whereas (iii) the related adenoid (NALT) does resolve distinct immature/mature M-cell clusters (Alvarez-Arguedas 2025).
